_partNote: Every class on this sheet is a battery, so the tiles are separated by cell format rather than by chemistry: an upright cylindrical can, a thin flat pouch with tabs, a tall prismatic can, a wide multi-cap block with tapered posts, a squat button disc, a two-tank flow skid, and a small axial-lead specialty cell. Aspect ratio and top furniture differ in every case, so no two silhouettes read the same at tile size.

partPrompts.1: A single cylindrical rechargeable cell standing upright on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a smooth round can with a crimped groove running around it just below the top, a small raised button terminal centered on the flat top face, and plain unmarked sides. One bold object and nothing else in the frame: no wires, no printing, no holder, and not a bare featureless tube — the crimped groove and the raised terminal must read clearly.
partPrompts.2: A single flat laminated pouch cell lying tilted on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a thin rectangular slab with a wide flat sealed flange running all the way around its edge, the middle section slightly domed, and two flat rectangular tabs standing out side by side from one short edge. It should read as thin and soft-walled, not as a rigid can. No cylinder, no terminal posts, no wires, no printing.
partPrompts.3: A single hard prismatic cell standing upright, seen three-quarter: a thin-walled rectangular can noticeably taller than it is wide, with softly rounded vertical corners and a flat top face carrying two short round terminals set near the ends and one narrow scored vent strip between them. One object only. Not a squat multi-cell block, no screw caps, no carry handle, no wrapper.
partPrompts.4: A squat multi-cell block battery seen three-quarter, clearly wider than it is tall: a rectangular molded case with a row of six round screw-in vent caps along the flat top, two tapered round posts standing at one end of that top face, and shallow molded ribs down the sides. The row of caps and the pair of tapered posts are the identifying geometry. One object, no cables, no charger, no cutaway.
partPrompts.5: A single small button cell lying flat, seen three-quarter: a thick coin-shaped can much wider than it is tall, with a clear stepped rim where the top cap crimps over the lower can, and three small round air holes grouped in the middle of the flat top face. It should read as a squat disc, not as a can standing on end. No wrapper, no printing, no wires, nothing beside it.
partPrompts.6: Two tall upright cylindrical liquid tanks standing side by side on a low rectangular skid, with a much smaller flat rectangular block sitting between them at skid level and one short straight pipe running from each tank to that block. The pair of large tanks dominates and the small block is clearly secondary. Simple shapes only: no valves, no fine plumbing, no cutaway, no cells.
partPrompts.7: A single small sealed cell lying on its side on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a short stubby cylindrical can with flat welded end caps and one stiff straight wire lead extending outward from the center of each end, like an axial electronic component. The two axial leads are the identifying feature. Not an upright cell, no crimped shoulder, no button terminal, no wrapper, no printing.
